conventions.convention: Complex inner products are linear in the first argument. Component-valued L² consists of almost-everywhere equivalence classes, with pairing ∫Σ f_l conjugate(g_l).
The orthogonal sums are finite, indexed by 1,…,r with r≥1; the norm of a bounded sum is the maximum of the component norms, including zero component spaces.
Q_j is multiplication by x_j on its maximal L² domain; P_k=−iℏD_k on classes whose kth weak derivative belongs to L². The CCR is asserted on componentwise Schwartz functions.
Fourier transformation uses exp(−2πix·ξ). Momentum coordinates are p=2πℏξ, and the unitary momentum transform has kernel (2πℏ)^(−d/2) exp(−ip·x/ℏ).
The massive model has m>0, s∈{0,1/2,1,…}, r=2s+1 and three spatial dimensions. Position, momentum and spin have units m, kg m s⁻¹ and J s respectively; ℏ remains explicit.
T_a f(x)=f(x−a); the passive chart change is x′=x+a. The position law shifts by +a, while T_a Q_j T_a⁻¹=Q_j−a_jI.
B_u(t)f(x)=exp(i(mu·x−m|u|²t/2)/ℏ)f(x−ut). Its chart change is x′=x+ut, whose new chart moves at velocity −u. Position and momentum laws shift by ut and mu.
The Gaussian width parameter σ is positive; the coordinate variance is σ²/2, and the momentum width parameter is σ_p=ℏ/σ.
The plane-wave functional is conjugate-linear: u_k(φ)=∫exp(ik·x) conjugate(φ(x)) dx. It is a Schwartz functional, not a normalizable state.
The confined warning uses 0<L<∞ and the momentum domain consisting of H¹ classes with both endpoint traces zero; its adjoint has the whole H¹ domain.

load_bearing.statement: Under P1, P2, P5 and P6, for m>0 and s∈{0,1/2,1,…}, the one-particle Hilbert space is H_s=L²(R³;C^(2s+1)); position and momentum are the componentwise maximal-domain operators Q_j and P_k, spin acts by the matrices ℏJ_i, and the momentum representative is U^(s)ψ with the stated Fourier normalization and units.

Assuming Countable Choice and Choice, for d,r≥1 and ℏ>0, the componentwise maximal-domain Q_j and P_k on L²(R^d;C^r) are densely defined and self-adjoint. Fourier transformation sends P_k to multiplication by 2πℏξ_k. Translations preserve the displayed domains and satisfy T_aQ_jT_a⁻¹=Q_j−a_jI and T_aP_kT_a⁻¹=P_k; T_(te_j)=exp(−itP_j/ℏ).

Assuming Countable Choice and Choice, for d,r≥1 and ℏ>0, U^(r) is unitary from L²(dx;C^r) to L²(dp;C^r), carries D(P_k) onto D(M_(p_k)) and intertwines P_k with M_(p_k). On Schwartz functions U^(r)Q_j=iℏ∂_(p_j)U^(r); on the whole Hilbert space U^(r)T_aU^(r)⁻¹=M_exp(−ia·p/ℏ).

Under P2, P5, P6, Countable Choice and Choice, the spin-s model's coordinate position and momentum laws in a unit vector ψ are the integrals of ‖ψ(x)‖² and ‖U^(s)ψ(p)‖² over the respective coordinate bins. The unique regular joint position PVM is G(B)=M_(1_B). Coordinate laws are atomless, both coordinate spectra equal R, and internal unitary matrix actions preserve the coordinate laws.

Assuming Countable Choice and Choice, the componentwise Schwartz space is invariant under Q_j and P_k and satisfies [Q_j,P_k]f=iℏδ_jk f. Every constant matrix action S_× is bounded with norm ‖S‖, preserves the individual operator domains, commutes there with the spatial operators and commutes with their explicitly identified spectral PVMs; under Θ it is I⊗S.

Assuming Countable Choice, for d,r≥1, the finite direct sum of scalar L² spaces and the completed tensor product L²(R^d)⊗̂C^r are unitarily identified with component-valued L². The tensor identification intertwines bounded scalar multiplication and translation with their bounded tensor amplifications.

Assuming Countable Choice, a finite orthogonal sum of densely defined self-adjoint operators on complex Hilbert spaces is densely defined and self-adjoint on the displayed component domain. A finite sum of bounded operators has norm max_l‖B_l‖, adjoint ⊕B_l*, and is unitary when all its components are unitary.

Under its stated postulates and choice hypotheses, translations transport position laws by +a, preserve momentum laws, conjugate H_V to H_(V(·−a)) on componentwise W²,², and conjugate their unitary flows. For bounded measurable V, invariance under every translation is equivalent to V being constant almost everywhere.

concerns.concern: F4 says 'Change of variables under a translation holds for integrable functions' and cites thm-linear-change-of-variables-for-lebesgue-measure. That supplier states a result for linear maps, whereas x↦x−a is affine for a≠0. Step 3.1 uses this translation substitution. The calculation is correct, but the cited statement does not supply it; a translation-invariance argument or the available C¹ change-of-variables supplier closes the gap.

Definition (e) calls the transformation law of state representatives 'a derived statement about the model’s operators' and says it is not an additional assumption. The covariance theorems instead explicitly choose the representative readings T_a and B_u(t), then derive their covariance identities. Distinguish the chosen representative/frame convention from the identities proved conditional on that choice; the operator calculations do not establish a unique representative transformation law.

alerts.finding: F1 says the product-domain conditions are 'that is x_j D_j f∈L² and D_j(x_j f)∈L² ...; no other hypothesis enters the definitions of the product domains.' This abbreviation drops f∈D(P_j) and f∈D(Q_j), which Statement (b) correctly includes. For d=r=1, f(x)=(1+x²)^(−1/2) belongs to L² and has xf′ and (xf)′ in L², but xf∉L², so PQf is undefined. The cited kinematics supplier retains the operand-domain conditions. Statement (b) and the proof restore them; F1 needs an explicit qualification.

The supplier page qm-math-orbital-and-spin incorrectly summarizes this item: after displaying J_z and J_± it says 'the standard matrices ... are self-adjoint'. For s=1/2, J_+=[[0,1],[0,0]] is not self-adjoint. The item itself correctly states that J_z,J_x,J_y are self-adjoint and J_+*=J_−. This finding concerns the owning page’s summary, not a defect in the proposition’s Statement.
